# A Look at Disrupted Software Stocks

Report 182 | Published 2026-02-15 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2026-2-15/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/182.json)

Software moats, capex and valuation.

The article accurately documents the Valaris catalyst and several relative-performance observations. Its strongest explanations distinguish capital intensity from accounting profits. Adobe business resilience has support but its equity lagged at the audit cutoff. Broad AI-surplus and equal-weight claims remain insufficiently specified for clean forecast scoring.

**Coverage:** Full numbered text and image inventory read. All material theses across macro, digital assets, investment analysis and concluding sections considered. Position listings and incidental descriptive statistics are excluded unless they support a thesis.

## Claims

### 182-C01

**Reserve purchases ease funding pressure.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | reserve-management-funding |
| Source blocks | 8 |
| Thesis family | reserve-management-funding |

Technical reserve supply and the stated ample-reserve objective are verified. Attributing all improvement in interbank conditions to those purchases requires SOFR spreads and other funding controls; balance-sheet expansion is not synonymous with risk-asset stimulus.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [Reserve management purchase announcement](https://www.newyorkfed.org/markets/opolicy/operating_policy_251210a) | New York Fed | 2025-12-10 | Verified in the audit

Purchases began December 12, 2025 to maintain ample reserves; initial monthly amount about $40 billion. Technical reserve supply does not itself establish a change in the interest-rate stance.

- [Early experience with reserve management purchases](https://www.newyorkfed.org/newsevents/speeches/2026/per260326) | New York Fed | 2026-03-26 | Verified in the audit

The Desk purchased about $40 billion monthly ahead of expected April tax flows. The objective was maintaining ample reserves.

### 182-C03

**Weaker dollars help foreign borrowers.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | dollar-debt-financial-channel |
| Source blocks | 14 |

The local-currency cost of fixed dollar debt falls when the dollar depreciates, assuming unchanged local earnings and no offsetting hedge. This bounded balance-sheet channel does not prove all emerging markets benefit equally.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Fixed USD liabilities
- Local-currency revenues unchanged
- Unhedged exposure

Local liability value is USD liability times local units/USD; dollar depreciation reduces that product.

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.

### 182-C17

**AI capex reduces distributable cash.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Right |
| Type | explanation |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | ai-capex-free-cash flow |
| Source blocks | 105, 141, 143 |
| Thesis family | ai-capex-free-cashflow |

For a given operating cash flow, higher capital spending reduces current free cash flow arithmetically. The identity does not establish poor lifetime returns: future revenue, depreciation, utilization and financing must be evaluated.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Deductive assessment:**

- Operating cash flow fixed
- Free cash flow defined as operating cash flow less capex

Increasing the subtracted capex term reduces current free cash flow one-for-one; future cash flows are not constrained by this identity.

**Outcome evidence:**

No independent outcome source is recorded. Any deductive assessment is identified separately.

### 182-C21

**Equal weighting historically benefits from size/value.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | empirical |
| Horizon | Not specified |
| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |
| Asset or variable | equal-weight-history |
| Source blocks | 139, 140 |
| Thesis family | equal-weight-history |

S&P’s research supports the smaller-size, value and anti-momentum tilts and historical equal-weight outperformance in its long samples. The live index began in January 2003; earlier decades are backtests. Entry endpoint, fees and turnover affect investor results, and subsequent mega-cap leadership can reverse long-window rankings. Historical attribution does not guarantee the next rotation.

**Direction:** See assessment; evidence is limited to the stated proposition.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Price direction alone does not identify causation.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Outcome evidence:**

- [S&P 500 Equal Weight FAQ](https://www.spglobal.com/spdji/en/education/article/sp-500-equal-weight-index-faq/) | S&P Dow Jones Indices | 2026-04-20 | Verified in the audit
